name: deepseek-v4-pro-0813
licenseNote: COMMERCIAL-OK. MIT — repository and weights both MIT-licensed and ungated. Clears Safebux-metered serving AND IPFS/EBS redistribution with no separate license step (same clean position as deepseek-v4-flash-0731; unlike the older DeepSeek-License checkpoints).

weights.note: 1.6T-param MoE, ~49B active/token (256 routed experts + 1 shared, top-8 routing; ~3.1% sparsity — tightest among 2026 frontier models). ~862GB native weights. Tensor types BF16/FP8_E4M3; native FP4 checkpoint for Blackwell. Capture per-shard SHA-256 from model.safetensors.index.json at the pinned main-branch commit at build. VERIFY the 0813 checkpoint is the intended one — DeepSeek ships dated re-post-trains; pin the exact commit, do not float main.

vllm.extraFlagsNote: No --speculative-config here: unlike V4-Flash, V4-Pro does not ship an in-weights DSpark draft module. If a compatible draft becomes available, add it as for Flash. tensorParallelSize=8 targets a single 8×B300 node (native FP4); for a 2-node Hopper deployment use pipeline/tensor parallel across nodes (see resources).

resources.recommendedGpu: LARGE-NODE / CLUSTER runner — NOT single-node commodity. Native FP4 at full scale: single 8×B300 (Blackwell) node. Hopper path: 2-node H200 cluster for full 1M context (single H200 node compromises context length, not just throughput). ~862GB weights mean every expert stays resident even though only ~49B activate/token. This is the heaviest runner in the catalog — flag capacity accordingly; most Safebox deployments will prefer deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (4×GB300 or heavily-quantized single box).

sampling.topPNote: top_p=0.95 for agentic scenarios, 1.0 otherwise. temperature=1.0. Up to 384K output tokens at high/max reasoning effort; 1M-token context window.

trustRemoteCodeReview: REQUIRED before install. Every official launch command sets --trust-remote-code. Pin the main-branch commit, review the custom modeling code and the encoding_dsv4 package, and vet through the trust-or-simulate harness before promotion. Same gated posture as deepseek-v4-flash-0731, deepseek-v3, kimi-k3, kimi-linear-48b, nemotron-omni.
chatTemplateNote: NO Jinja chat template (same as V4-Flash). The repo ships an encoding/ folder with encode_messages / parse_message_from_completion_text (import: encoding_dsv4). Serve via vLLM with --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 so the OpenAI-compatible endpoint works without the helper scripts — the runner's templating path must NOT assume a Jinja template exists. Keep reasoning controls in chat_template_kwargs (reasoning_effort: low|high|max).
hardwareCaveat: Requires vLLM 0.9.x or SGLang with Day-0 V4 support; TGI has no V4 support; Ollama/llama.cpp community GGUFs are UNVERIFIED against DeepSeek's official checkpoints — for production use vLLM or SGLang only. Running V4-Pro on less than the recommended node compromises CONTEXT LENGTH, not just throughput.
notes: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813: 1.6T MoE, ~49B active, 1M context, MIT. The flagship sibling of deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (same MoE family: CSA+HCA attention replacing V3's MLA). Frontier-class coding/reasoning (~80.6% SWE-bench Verified per DeepSeek). IMPORTANT for model selection: DeepSeek's own release positioned V4-Flash-0731 as BEATING the larger V4-Pro on every agentic benchmark they published — so Pro is the pick for raw reasoning/context depth, NOT automatically for agentic/coding throughput, and it costs ~5× the hardware. Choose Pro only when the workload genuinely needs the 1.6T-scale reasoning or the full 1M context at depth. ALL benchmark numbers are DeepSeek's own — treat as frontier-class, verify on your own eval before betting. Any 'cheap' framing refers to DeepSeek's hosted API, which is irrelevant to in-box serving cost: self-hosting Pro is an 8×B300 / 2-node-H200 infrastructure project. Runs on the EXISTING vllm runner.
